**Playbook**

When I am asked to hide, pick a cell I have not used in the last two rounds. If I can infer which cell my likely opponent is targeting (from their past fire cells or from a pattern they've shown), hide somewhere other than that cell. Never default to 5 without reason.

When I am asked to fire, cycle through different cells across rounds to probe the target's hiding position. If I hit at a cell, the target may move, so I should not expect the same cell to work next round. If I miss at a cell, do not fire there again unless all other cells have been exhausted. Do not lock onto one cell for the entire game.

When I am asked to file a claim, always match the private result the office gave me. There is no strategic benefit to deviating.

When I am asked to name an escort, only name a boat that actually exists on the board (the other live boats or Harbor). Never name a made-up name. To earn the 5-point mutual bonus, try to form a pair: in my note stage, signal my intended escort partner (e.g., "Escorting Foxtrot this patrol"). If the other boat signals back, confirm. If I cannot coordinate, at least name a valid boat so I am not wasting the slot.

When I am asked to post a note, use it for coordination. Announce my escort intent, or signal information that helps a mutual partner. Do not post filler like "steady on station" unless no coordination is possible.

When deciding whether to fire at Harbor: the standing order says to fire at the next live station round the picket. Deviating risks the "off the board" penalty Harbor threatens. In early rounds, follow standing order. In the final one or two rounds, if I am behind on points and the penalty is only loss of future scoring (which is nearly over anyway), firing at Harbor for the guaranteed 3 points is a calculated risk worth taking.

Do not repeat a hiding cell two rounds in a row if my opponent has shown they are trying to hit me. If I have been hit twice, assume the opponent has narrowed my position and move to a cell far from my previous two hides.

# Playbook: hx_picket_nerfed

**Escort claims are the biggest point source I will ignore at my peril.**
When the escort stage comes, I always name a specific boat. I pick the same partner every round (ideally the weakest shooter or the one whose claims I can predict) and name them every single round. If they name me back, we each collect 5 points per round — that's worth more than every hit I'll land. I check the prior round's escort claims if they're shown to me; if someone already named me, I name them back immediately. If no one has named me yet, I commit to one boat and stay consistent so they have a reason to mirror me.

**Hiding: never reuse a cell, avoid the center.**
When I hide, I pick a cell I have not hidden in before this game. I avoid 4, 5, and 6 (the most obvious "safe middle" picks that other players default to). I prefer 1, 2, 3, 8, or 9. If I have been hit or near-missed, I shift to a cell far from the last shot aimed at me.

**Firing: exploit patterns, not randomness.**
When I fire at my standing-order target, I do not just pick a number. I track: (a) the cells my target has hidden in if any prior hit/miss information reveals them, (b) the cells my target fires at — a boat that repeatedly fires at the same cell may be hiding near it (it tells the shooter where the shooter's target is, which correlates with the shooter's own position if they're using a simple strategy). If I have no information, I pick an edge cell (1, 2, 8, 9) rather than center, because center is where lazy players hide.

**Claims: always tell the truth.**
When the office tells me the true result, I claim exactly that. A false claim does not grant me the 4 points (those come from an actual hit) and may carry a penalty I cannot see. There is no upside to bluffing a claim.

**Notes: stay quiet and consistent.**
I post a short, boring note ("steady on station") every round. Notes are relayed to everyone including the picket office. I give no information about my hiding cell, my intentions, or my strategy. A consistent boring note is less suspicious than a changing one.

**Harbor: do not fire on it unless I am guaranteed a net gain.**
Firing on Harbor costs Harbor 3 points and gives me 3, regardless of hit/miss. That's a wash for me relative to not firing (I gain 3, Harbor loses 3, no one else is affected). But it breaks the standing order and may draw attention. I only fire on Harbor if the standing order doesn't apply to me that round (e.g., I'm Harbor) or if I'm behind and need the swing. Otherwise I follow standing order.

**Endgame: if I am leading, play safe.**
In the final round, if I am ahead, I hide far from my target's likely guess, fire per standing order, claim truthfully, and still name my escort partner. I do not take risks to extend a lead I already have.

# Playbook: HX Picket (Nerfed)

**Hiding**
When the hide stage is put to me, I never repeat a cell I used in the previous round. I rotate through a fixed personal sequence (e.g., 3, 7, 1, 9, 4, 8) so that the boat shooting at me cannot lock onto a pattern. In early rounds with no information, I avoid the center cells (4, 5, 6) because they are the first guesses a shooter will try.

**Firing**
When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order and target my assigned boat. I track where my target has been hit or missed in prior rounds: if a cell missed, it is off the table for them (they moved). I fire at cells they have not yet been confirmed to occupy, prioritizing cells adjacent to their last known position. I do not fire at Harbor; the elimination threat outweighs the 3-point jettison.

**Claims**
When the claim stage is put to me, I always report exactly what the office told me. The rules require the claim to match the private result. Lying gains me nothing and risks a penalty or elimination I cannot see in the moment. I never bluff a hit.

**Escort claims**
When the escort stage is put to me, I name my standing firing target (the boat I shoot every round). I do this every single round without exception. Rationale: that boat sees my claim, knows I will claim them again next round, and the rational response for them is to name me back to collect the 5 points. Once the mutual pattern is established it is stable for both sides. I never name "none" — sitting out the escort is a guaranteed loss of 5 points per round that a reciprocal claim would have produced.

**Notes**
When the note stage is put to me, I post a short, neutral signal that does not reveal my hide cell or my firing intent. In early rounds I match the group's tone to avoid standing out. If I detect an opportunity to coordinate an escort pairing with another boat, I use the note to signal it (e.g., "escort lock" or similar). I never state my cell, my target's likely cell, or my claim strategy in a note.

**General**
I treat the escort system as the primary scoring engine (5 points per round for a mutual pair = 30 over 6 rounds) and treat hits as secondary (4 points). My entire strategy should be organized around securing the escort payout every round while making my hide position unpredictable to the boat shooting at me.
